profile.name: Joselito Villanueva Dizon
profile.role: Enterprise Architect · AI Systems Architect · Solution Architect
profile.statement: Making AI practical, personal, and meaningful in everyday life.
about: Experienced technology architect passionate about AI and innovation. I design and build AI systems end to end — from the model and the data to the API, the interface and the server it runs on.

MealSenseAI and CEREBRO were both developed as MVPs during my postgraduate studies in AI Systems at NUS — MealSenseAI applying machine learning, computer vision and conversational AI, CEREBRO knowledge representation and reasoning. Both run their AI on local models.

projects.name: MealSenseAI
projects.tagline: Nutrition intelligence from a photo of your meal.
projects.description: Photograph a meal and MealSenseAI segments the plate, identifies each food and estimates its nutrition, showing how it reached every number. A Meal Advisor answers questions grounded in your own logged meals, and glucose-impact estimates in mmol/L are always labelled as estimates, never as measurements.
highlights: YOLO11 segmentation with an EfficientNet-B0 food classifier (Food-101 + FoodSG)
Explainable pipeline: every estimate shows its source and confidence
Grounded Meal Advisor on a local LLM via Ollama

demo.summary: A five-minute narrated tour: why unlabelled meals are the gap in diabetes self-care, then one hawker lunch from photo to portions, glucose impact, a portion and walking what-if, and the Meal Advisor.
demo.note: Wei Ming and his meals are fictional. What you see is the real application and its real output. Educational estimates only, not medical advice.

projects.name: Food Recognition Model
projects.tagline: A 320-class food classifier, from 310,861 audited images.
projects.description: Two public datasets (Food-101 and FoodSG) merged into one 320-class taxonomy, audited for leakage and conflicting labels, and used to fine-tune EfficientNet-B0 on a self-hosted GPU. It reaches 70.6% top-1 and 85.7% top-3 accuracy on 45,800 held-out test images, and powers MealSenseAI's meal recognition.
highlights: 70.6% top-1 and 85.7% top-3 accuracy on 45,800 held-out images
Trained and evaluated on my own GPU (RTX 5060 Ti, 16 GB)

projects.name: CEREBRO
projects.tagline: Adaptive Knowledge and Reasoning Digital Twin.
projects.description: CEREBRO turns personal documents and experience into a private, connected knowledge store — Learn, Connect, Reason, Recall. It ingests PDF, Word, PowerPoint and Markdown, proposes metadata for human approval, and answers questions with citations back to the exact fragment. A Galaxy view maps how topics connect; a Timeline orders what the documents themselves date.
highlights: Enrichment proposes, a person approves — provenance on every field
Hybrid keyword and semantic recall with local embeddings
Ask with citations, on a local model — no cloud AI engine

demo.summary: A five-minute narrated tour: adding a document, search, the Knowledge Galaxy, the Timeline and Ask CEREBRO, on the documents of a fictional company.
demo.note: Larkspur Logistics and everything about it are invented. What you see is the real application and real output from local models.

projects.name: Knowledge Search Evaluation
projects.tagline: Search, topics and cited answers, tested on public benchmarks.
projects.description: How well CEREBRO searches, groups topics and answers questions, measured on SciFact, 20 Newsgroups and SQuAD 2.0 on my own GPU. With the models it was designed for, search scores 0.73 nDCG@10, three times the live setup, and 93% of answers cite the right source.
highlights: 93% of answers cite the right source

projects.name: Image Understanding Evaluation
projects.tagline: Naming, captioning and linking images, tested on ImageNetV2.
projects.description: Can CEREBRO describe images and find related ones on its own? On 100 ImageNetV2 photos, ResNet-50 names the subject 71% of the time (89% within its top five), every image gets a Florence-2 caption, and the top similar image is relevant 65% of the time: useful suggestions that a person still reviews.
highlights: Top similar image relevant 65% of the time

projects.name: NEXUS
projects.description: An architecture workbench where architects design cloud, hybrid and on-premises systems grounded in their organisation's own policies, controls and architecture standards. It simulates infrastructure on the fly across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and on-premises data centres: load and scaling behaviour, what-if analyses (traffic spikes, zone and region outages, failover), resilience-pattern comparisons and cost estimates. AI agents review each design against the ground truth, and an architect approves every change. The AI runs on a local small language model (SLM), with a larger LLM for second opinions.
highlights: Grounded in ground truth: policies, controls and architecture standards checked by rule
On-the-fly simulation across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and on-premises: load, scaling, outages, failover and cost
AI agents review and propose; the architect approves every change
